description: Observe and diagnose dynamic upgrade signals on the local Base devnet: L1 schedules, EL/CL propagation, live apply failures, and read health.

options.content:
# 🔵 Base Devnet · Dynamic Upgrades
Follow **L1 ProtocolVersions → EL / CL observations → live apply**. Devnet defaults to `runtime-admin`; `metrics-only` observes without applying and `startup-apply` applies only at startup.

**Observed does not mean applied or ready.** Activation `0` means unscheduled; positive values are L2 Unix seconds. Upgrade labels are names (`azul`, `denim`, …). Protocol versions encode `major × 1,000,000 + minor × 1,000 + patch` (`1001000` = v1.1.0).

**Missing telemetry is not healthy zero.** Apply gauges appear only after an attempt; counter rates can miss first events (see raw counters). Fail-closed may exit before scraping: check availability and fatal logs. Availability ignores layer/upgrade filters; empty-schedule reads ignore the upgrade filter.

panels.title: Triage · Availability, observation, and live-apply state

panels.description: Fraction of selected Prometheus node targets reachable. Reachability does not prove the upgrade poller is active; layer/upgrade filters do not apply.
panels.title: Reachable nodes

panels.description: Count of selected node/layer pairs with successful-read telemetry. Compare with your selected topology; a missing poller must not be inferred healthy.
panels.title: Reporting readers

panels.description: Number of selected per-upgrade apply-failure gauges raised. One failed schedule can raise multiple upgrades. Absence also occurs before the first live apply; zero is not a readiness verdict.
panels.title: Failing series

panels.description: Upgrades with differing observed activation timestamps across selected instances AND layers. Requires at least two reporting series; keep both layers and all nodes selected for fleet comparison.

targets.expr: sum(((max by (upgrade) (reth_base_upgrade_signal_activation_timestamp{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance",layer=~"$layer",upgrade=~"$upgrade"}) - min by (upgrade) (reth_base_upgrade_signal_activation_timestamp{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance",layer=~"$layer",upgrade=~"$upgrade"})) and on (upgrade) (count by (upgrade) (reth_base_upgrade_signal_activation_timestamp{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance",layer=~"$layer",upgrade=~"$upgrade"}) > 1)) > bool 0)

panels.title: Divergent upgrades

panels.description: Observed counter increases in the dashboard range; can miss the first event or process exit before scrape. No telemetry is not zero events.
panels.title: Halts · range

panels.description: Sum of per-node/layer failed-read increases, deduplicated across upgrade labels. A shared read may still be reported by both layers. First events may be missed.
panels.title: Read errors · range
Observed L1 schedule · Per-node values, not proof of application

panels.description: Each selected node and layer retains its own observed schedule. Zero means unscheduled, not the Unix epoch. Positive times may already be in the past.
panels.title: Activation schedule · L2 Unix seconds

panels.description: Sticky result of the most recent live apply: 1 = failing; 0 = successful. Absent before any apply attempt. A process exit can remove the gauge; use availability and logs.
panels.title: Latest live apply state · Per upgrade

panels.description: Raw L2 Unix timestamps read from L1. Step changes show observations, not successful local application. Zero means unscheduled.
panels.title: Observed activation timestamp

panels.description: Encoded minimum protocol version: major × 1,000,000 + minor × 1,000 + patch. This gauge does not expose the node binary version or establish readiness.
panels.title: Expected minimum protocol version
Propagation · Compare every selected node and both layers

panels.description: Difference across all selected nodes AND layers for each upgrade. Zero means agreement among reporters only. At least two series are required; missing reporters are not detected by this comparison.

targets.expr: (max by (upgrade) (reth_base_upgrade_signal_activation_timestamp{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance",layer=~"$layer",upgrade=~"$upgrade"}) - min by (upgrade) (reth_base_upgrade_signal_activation_timestamp{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance",layer=~"$layer",upgrade=~"$upgrade"})) and on (upgrade) (count by (upgrade) (reth_base_upgrade_signal_activation_timestamp{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance",layer=~"$layer",upgrade=~"$upgrade"}) > 1)

panels.title: Activation disagreement · max − min

panels.description: Difference in encoded protocol minimum across all selected nodes AND layers. Requires two reporting series; no data is not agreement.

targets.expr: (max by (upgrade) (reth_base_upgrade_signal_expected_protocol_version{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance",layer=~"$layer",upgrade=~"$upgrade"}) - min by (upgrade) (reth_base_upgrade_signal_expected_protocol_version{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance",layer=~"$layer",upgrade=~"$upgrade"})) and on (upgrade) (count by (upgrade) (reth_base_upgrade_signal_expected_protocol_version{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance",layer=~"$layer",upgrade=~"$upgrade"}) > 1)

panels.title: Protocol-version disagreement · max − min

panels.description: Number of selected node/layer series observed for each upgrade. A drop can make divergence disappear without convergence. This is not an expected-topology coverage check.
panels.title: Schedule reporters per upgrade

panels.description: Lowest last-read block across the selected upgrades for each node/layer. A stalled line may indicate polling/read failures or a stalled L1; this is block progress, not a last-read wall-clock timestamp.
panels.title: Last successful L1 read block
Diagnostics · Counter rates and recorded events

panels.description: Observed live value changes per upgrade, not successful applies. Counters appear on first event; rates require two samples.
panels.title: Observed signal updates

panels.description: Failed schedule attempts per second, deduplicated across upgrades. Applies affect the whole schedule and increment every included upgrade. Missing counters do not prove success.
panels.title: Live apply failures

panels.description: Failed read attempts per second, deduplicated across upgrade labels. A single read failure increments every known upgrade; shared reads can appear in both layers.
panels.title: L1 read errors

panels.description: Successful reads returning an empty schedule are rejected, leaving the previous live schedule in place. This layer-only metric intentionally ignores the upgrade filter.
panels.title: Empty L1 schedules

panels.description: Best-effort observed event increases over the rate window. The process can exit before scraping or after the first sample, so a blank/zero chart does not rule out a halt. Check node logs and reachability.
panels.title: Fail-closed events

panels.description: Prometheus scrape success for each selected node target. Independent of layer/upgrade selection. A missing target or absent metric is not a successful scrape.
panels.title: Node target availability

panels.description: Raw current counter values retain the first recorded event that rates can miss. Counters reset on process restart and are not range totals. L1 errors and apply failures duplicate schedule events per upgrade: do not sum these rows. Empty-schedule rows have no upgrade label and ignore that filter.
panels.title: Recorded per-upgrade event counters · Since process start
